newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Oct industrial output falls 6.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Oct industrial output falls 6.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Bulgarian state industrial output fell by 6.5 percent in October against the same month last year after a 12 percent fall in September, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said.

Output fell due to a drop in the lev against the dollar, high interest rates, soaring inflation, insolvency of clients and the declining number of orders from domestic and foreign clients, the NSI said in a statement.

Industrial production in the state sector totalled 182 billion levs in October. It amounted to 1,028 billion levs for the first 10 months of 1996, down a real three percent from the same period of 1995, NSI figures showed.
Industrial production in both the state and the private sectors in October amounted to some 208 billion levs, which was a real 5 percent down from the same month last year, figures showed.

The private industrial sector posted a real 10 percent rise in output year-on-year in October but the rise could not compensate the fall in the state sector as output in the private sector accounted for around 13 percent of the total.
The largest decrease in output was posted in food and beverages industry, chemical and oil-processing industry and ferrous metallurgy, the NSI said.

In October the lev fell from 225 to 245 to the dollar, the central bank's main interest rate ranged between 300 and 240 percent and monthly consumer price inflation was 16.7 percent -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
